title: Decoherence is far too fast for brain quantum computation

statements.text: Decoherence in neurons and in microtubule excitations takes 10^-13 to 10^-20 seconds, far shorter than the 10^-3 to 10^-1 seconds of neural dynamics, so the brain’s cognitive degrees of freedom are classical, against Penrose’s suggestion.

Decoherence in neurons and in microtubule excitations takes $10^{-13}$ to $10^{-20}$ seconds, far shorter than the $10^{-3}$ to $10^{-1}$ seconds of neural dynamics, so the brain’s cognitive degrees of freedom are classical, against Penrose’s suggestion.

sources.quote: This conclusion disagrees with suggestions by Penrose and others that the brain acts as a quantum computer, and that quantum coherence is related to consciousness in a fundamental way.
